title: A benchmark harness over seeds

blocks.text: A logistics team benchmarks its solvers on a fixed instance set with several seeds, the way lesson 5.4.2 built GridCap's harness. The solving itself is behind one function the team already has: `solve(solver, instance, seed)` returns `(solved, work)`, whether the run proved optimality and the solver's deterministic work count. `shifted_geometric_mean(values, shift)` is given in `harness.py`.
Write `benchmark(solve, solvers, instances, seeds, shift, cap)`. For every solver, instance and seed (a **cell**), call `solve` twice. Return, for each solver, a dict with:

items: `"solved"`: how many cells' first run solved;
`"repeat"`: `True` only if, in every cell, the two runs returned the same `(solved, work)`;
`"sgm"`: the shifted geometric mean, with `shift`, of the first runs' work, where a run that did not solve counts as `cap`.

blocks.text: The tests call it with a stand-in `solve`, so no solver runs. About twelve lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from harness import benchmark

# (solver, instance, seed) -> (solved, work units)
work = {
    ("Lynx", "yard-1", 3): (True, 250.0), ("Lynx", "yard-2", 3): (True, 4000.0),
    ("Lynx", "yard-1", 4): (True, 300.0), ("Lynx", "yard-2", 4): (True, 3600.0),
    ("Puma", "yard-1", 3): (True, 600.0), ("Puma", "yard-2", 3): (False, 90000.0),
    ("Puma", "yard-1", 4): (True, 650.0), ("Puma", "yard-2", 4): (True, 1500.0),
}
result = benchmark(lambda s, i, k: work[s, i, k], ["Lynx", "Puma"], ["yard-1", "yard-2"], [3, 4], 100.0, 1e5)
for solver, row in result.items():
    print(f"{solver}: runs {row['runs']}, solved {row['solved']}, repeat {row['repeat']}, sgm {round(row['sgm'], 1)}")

cases.says: each solver's summary has its run count and the shifted geometric mean of its work over the instances
every seed of every instance is run and enters the mean
a run that does not solve counts at the cap instead of being dropped, and is not counted as solved
each cell runs twice, and a solver whose two runs of a cell differ is marked as not repeating

origin.section: Measure Deterministic Work Where You Can, and Mask Wall Time Where You Cannot

concepts: deterministic counts summarized per solver, failures at the cap, repeats checked
fix the instance set before the first run and report on all of it
several seeds per instance, each (instance, seed) one observation
